newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Refining reviews costs, distribution options.
newsitem.headline: NZ Refining reviews costs, distribution options.

text.p: The New Zealand Refining Co Ltd is looking at ways to expand the capacity of its distribution system into the Auckland marketplace, general manager Graham Searle said on Tuesday.

"These studies are at an early stage of development. On current industry estimates we expect the existing pipeline to match demand up until 2000/2001. Therefore we will need to seek additional capacity in the medium term," Searle told Reuters.
A news media report of a required investment of up to NZ$100 million was "purely speculative," he said.
"We would clearly proceed, subject to shareholder approval, with the most cost-effective, environmentally acceptable solution, whatever that may prove to be," he said.
But Searle said NZ$100 million would be a "ballpark" cost of building another pipeline. "But whether or not that is what we do is another matter of course."
The company at present operates a pipeline between its Marsden Point refinery and a terminal in South Auckland.
Aside from a new pipeline, other options would include a rail link and expanding coastal shipping facilities.
In NZ Refining's annual report, the company talked of two reviews currently under way, which address cost reduction and opportunities for enhancing profitability.
The company's annual manpower cost is NZ$26 million, with costs of contributions to employee schemes and travel expenses.
But its manpower cost, with the addition of contractors, comes closer to NZ$40 million.
"When we are looking at cutting costs we are actually looking at a broader base than that, so the base we are looking at is NZ$40 million," Searle said.

"We are reducing our cost base but it's not just the wage bill. We are looking at all our other significant costs as well," Searle said. "I don't see it as a big deal. It's just something that any business, in a competitive environment, does on a regular basis," he said.
Just over half NZ Refining's production is in middle distillate and under 30 percent is in gasoline.

The company is owned by local units of Mobil Corp (19.20 percent), The British Petroleum Co Plc (23.66 percent) and Royal Dutch Petroleum Co (17.14 percent). Fletcher Challenge Petroleum, a unit of Fletcher Energy
has 14.20 percent and a further 11.35 percent is held by Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
NZ Refining, which holds its annual meeting in Whangarei on Thursday, traded today at NZ$29.00, down 40 cents, on very light volume.
